payload.methodology_note:
How this report works

What a signal is:
A signal documents a public-record connection between a financial contribution to an official's campaign committee and a vote cast by that official within a configurable time window. It does not assert that the donation influenced the vote.

Evidence tiers:
• Documented — FEC donation record + Senate roll call vote within the proximity window
• Corroborated — Documented + one additional public-record indicator (active lobbying registration OR jurisdictional industry match)
• Multi-source — Documented + two or more additional public-record indicators

What is not checked in this run:
• Regulations.gov comment dockets — credential not configured
• GovInfo congressional hearing witnesses — credential not configured

Confirmation standard:
A signal reaches "confirmed" status when identity is resolved, temporal direction is verified, and at least two independent public-record indicators are present. No signals in this run met that standard because two evidence channels were unavailable.

Source data:
• FEC: api.open.fec.gov — Federal Election Commission public disclosure
• Senate votes: senate.gov LIS XML — official Senate roll call record
• LDA: lda.gov — lobbying disclosure (API + public filing views; legacy lda.senate.gov URLs 404)
• All sources are public government records


Profiles of sitting judicial officers include allegations tagged by epistemic level. Findings tagged ALLEGED represent formal complaints or legal allegations and have not been adjudicated. Findings tagged CONTEXTUAL represent public discourse and have not been independently verified. All findings link directly to primary sources.

This report was generated by Open Case and cryptographically signed at the time of generation. The signature covers all signals, evidence references, source statuses, and this methodology note.
